title: Which expression gives the time to grind y kilograms of grain?
description: Leeza owns a flour mill that takes ten seconds to start and eight seconds for each kilogram of grain. The video builds the expression for the total time and checks it with three kilograms.
teaching_notes: One idea: a start that happens once is added, while a time for each kilogram is multiplied by the number of kilograms. Watch for students who multiply the start time with the grinding time.

video_script.why: A learner uses the method of the bill expression: a once-only part is added to a part that is a number times a letter.
video_script.substitution: The method of the bill expression, with the start time in place of the jaggery cost and the grinding time in place of the coconuts.
video_script.anchor: Leeza's flour mill that takes some time to start and then grinds the grain
video_script.payoff_line: The time is ten plus eight times y seconds

final_answer.spoken: the time is ten plus eight times y seconds

never_show: the finished expression 10 + 8 × y before the answer beat
maths_rules: The machine starts once and takes 10 seconds.
Grinding y kilograms takes 8 × y seconds.
The total time is 10 + 8 × y seconds.
video_script.design: One idea: a once-only time is added to a time for each kilogram times the number of kilograms. Assumes the bill expression. A timeline of blocks stays on the stage. No wrong idea is raised.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The time is ten plus eight times y seconds.
Exactly one of the five expressions in the book says this same thing.
